why: Tier-1 CI tooling, one file: scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py. No order path, no strategy config, no risk caps, no src/, no config/, no deploy/, no live-VM runtime file, and no register is written. R12 does not apply: the file is not in LANDING_MACHINERY -- verified against that list rather than assumed. It stops a JSON parse failure collapsing into 'no rows' on BOTH sides of the diff. MEASURED on origin/main @7f832e8c0 with a conflict marker in docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json (1574 rows): a corrupt HEAD copy printed three 'OK' lines and exited 0 over a file none of the three checks could read; a corrupt BASE copy blamed 393 PRE-EXISTING rows this diff never touched. The two sides are treated asymmetrically on purpose -- the head side REFUSES (there is no benign reading of 'grade this file' when it cannot be read), the base side SKIPS LOUDLY and blames nothing (a corrupt base is main's problem and the likeliest PR to meet it is the one repairing it, so refusing would block the repair), and the OK line names what it skipped so it cannot claim coverage it lacks. Proven both ways on the same trees: OLD rc=0 with three OK lines vs NEW rc=2 naming the file; OLD rc=1 blaming 393 rows vs NEW rc=0 blaming none. Four planted defects each red their own control, including the over-refusal direction (an empty-but-valid backlog must NOT be treated as unparseable). Clean tree unchanged on --base, --all and --self-test.
